### BLOG batch 2 common ground (added 260729-2) — folded in the SAME pass that logged the tensions

*⚠️ **Swept and folded in the same pass, per the §8 item 4 discipline; check C10 guards it. Noted is not logged, so they are here.*** ⛔⛔ **ALL OF IT IS 2014-2017 — UNDERGRADUATE AND PRE-SEMINARY, earlier than every other batch including BLOG batch 1. A warm 2015 statement is evidence that he wrote it warmly in 2015, at twenty-something, on a popular blog. Nothing here is a current position.**

- ⭐ **PRAYER CHANGES THE PRAY-ER, NOT GOD — AND IT IS THE EARLIEST THING IN THE PROJECT (BLOG-67, 2014-09-07).** He rejects the framing that prayer changes God's mind, puts the alternative as a reductio he answers himself, and holds instead that prayer **sanctifies, perfects, makes us want what God wants, and trains our minds to reflect God's mind** — valuing set forms because *"holier men and women"* wrote them, so that he may *"conform myself to the prayer, rather than the prayer conform to me."* **[Stated, BLOG-67]** **[Analysis]** **This is common ground with any confessional Reformed reader and it is not a near miss:** prayer as a means of sanctification rather than of informing or moving God is straightforwardly the Reformed account of petition, and he reaches it at twenty. **Credit it plainly.** ⛔ **Crediting it does NOT license deploying the finding toward warrant** — it is about prayer, not ceremonial, and its companion `BLOG-68` carries an inline do-not-deploy guard.
- ⭐ **THE PASTORAL CASE AGAINST EMOTION-CENTRED WORSHIP — AND THE STYLE/SUBSTANCE DISCIPLINE THAT COMES WITH IT (BLOG-59, 2016-10-28).** He argues that worship focused primarily on the emotions **trains us to treat our emotions as reality rather than as perceptions of reality**, and draws the pastoral consequence: if the emotions are our primary means of connecting to Ultimate Reality, we have no resource when they report that we are beyond help. **[Stated, BLOG-59]** **[Analysis]** **Both halves are creditable and the second is the one that matters.** He states **four separate times** that musical style is **not** his target — he met the same problem in *"boring old hymns"*, one **can** worship rightly with modern instruments, and emotions are **necessary**. ⚠️ **It is therefore also a caution, and the caution does not diminish the credit: any lever that reads his ceremonial preference as an aesthetic or style preference will meet a pre-formed, worked objection in writing from 2016** — the same shape as `BLOG-39`'s published objection to arguing from motive.
- ⭐ **RELIGION DEFENDED AS INSTITUTION, STRUCTURE AND DOCTRINE — AND THE LIST OF LEGITIMATE AUTHORITIES IS BROADER THAN EXPECTED (BLOG-64, 2015-05-27).** Against *"relationship not religion,"* a position he reports having held himself, he argues that something must have standing to say *you're wrong*, that institutions are **guard rails against heresy**, and that we must understand God **together, with the wisdom of his people across the centuries.** He separates being **wrong** from being **damned**. **[Stated, BLOG-64]** **[Analysis]** ⭐ **The creditable part is the limit, and it is the interesting part:** he names **a Confession** and **Scripture** among the legitimate loci of authority alongside apostolic succession and the creeds, and **explicitly names Presbyterians and Southern Baptists as possessing the thing he is defending.** ⛔ **A broad, ecumenical, function-level account of authority — not a claim about the formularies and not a claim about episcopacy.** ⚠️ **It cuts mildly AGAINST reading his ecclesiology as narrow in this period, which is worth knowing before any Bucket A framing rests on the opposite assumption.**
- ⭐ **THEOLOGY IS REQUIRED OF EVERYONE — "YOU DO HAVE TO BE A THEOLOGIAN" (BLOG-65, 2016-01-11; with the mind strand of BLOG-58, 2016-10-28).** Against whittling the faith down to a feeling, he holds that God deserves devotion entire — intellect and spirit and body — that **theology is incredibly practical**, and that while one need not be a scholastic, *"you do have to be a theologian."* `BLOG-58` names **willing ignorance** as a failure of worship in its own right. **[Stated, BLOG-65, BLOG-58]** **[Analysis]** **Straightforward common ground, and unprompted.** ⛔ **Crediting the mind strand of `BLOG-58` does NOT license its definitional sentence** (*"our worship is not worship unless…"*), **which carries an inline usage guard: that is a completeness criterion about the worshipper's faculties, not a warrant criterion about what may be done.**
- **SUNG WORDS FORM WHAT HEARERS BELIEVE, AND SHOULD BE CHOSEN WITH CARE (BLOG-66, 2016-01-15).** Arguing that hearers may well take a lyric to mean what its authors did not intend, he holds that **good intentions do not redeem words that lead people to reject Christ's teaching**, and calls for choosing worship songs carefully. **[Stated, BLOG-66]** **[Analysis]** **This half is common ground with any confessional Reformed reader** — the content of what a congregation sings is a doctrinal matter, not merely a pastoral or aesthetic one. ⛔ **The OTHER half of `BLOG-66` is not common ground and is not credited here: his concession that low-church worship is *"not necessarily unbiblical"* carries an inline do-not-deploy guard and cuts AGAINST the project's direction of travel. Crediting the first half does not license the second.**
- **BAPTISMAL REGENERATION, DEEP-HISTORY ANTECEDENTS (BLOG-48, 2015; BLOG-55, 2016).** Sacramental efficacy asserted against a symbolic reading (Romans 6; 1 Cor 10:16-17), and both baptismal regeneration and infant baptism argued from Irenaeus and Cyprian. **[Stated, BLOG-48, BLOG-55]** **[Analysis]** ⛔ **Logged for balance, not as a lever: the baptismal-regeneration lever is RETIRED** (register, `GV-38`), and `VP-3` already records that the pair **creates no opening** and that its `DELTA` is `UNCHANGED`. ⚠️ **Note the shape difference held at `VP-3`: these two ground the doctrine in Romans 6 and in the Fathers, and name no formulary at all, while `VP-3`'s THEN and NOW are both formulary-grounded. Same doctrine, different ground.**

⚠️ **NOT common ground from this batch, recorded so the sweep's negative results are visible rather than silent** — and the `BLOG-16` precedent from the last pass governs: **filing something here that is not shared ground flatters the section rather than balancing it.** **`BLOG-45`** (*lex orandi*) is the batch's highest-value finding and is **not** shared ground — it is a formation claim the project must be careful not to upgrade, and it carries its own guard. **`BLOG-47`** and **`BLOG-60`** (the incense findings) are ceremonial data under the heaviest guards in the batch and are **emphatically not** common ground. **`BLOG-52`** (deuterocanon) states Article 6's substance and is a **tension-adjacent** datum on DQ-1, not agreement. **`BLOG-63`** (assurance) is genuinely interesting and cuts in an unexpected direction, but **he locates assurance in the weekly declarative absolution**, which is precisely where a Reformed reader would differ — **filing it as common ground would misrepresent both men**, and its personal setting is under a binding handling note besides. **`BLOG-69`**, **`BLOG-70`** and **`BLOG-71`** are biographical or source-handling and carry no doctrinal content to credit.

### ⭐⭐ LS batch 5 (`batch2`) common ground (added 260829-4) — swept and folded in the SAME pass that logged the findings

**FIVE CREDITS.**

- ⭐⭐ **The formulary used as authority, five years before the class did it (`LS-77`).** Arguing his Eucharistic position he goes to the **First Book of Homilies' preface**, the **Catechism** and the **1662 words of administration**, and reads **Article XXXV** aloud when the Homilies' standing is questioned. **`DQ-1`'s complaint is that he affirms the Homilies without using them; `IP-20` and `IP-71` (2026) are the two known instances, and this is earlier than both.** ⛔ Credited as method, not as a position on anything contested.
- ⭐⭐ **The opposing Eucharistic position ruled defensible from the formularies, non-heretical, and publicly argued by him (`LS-81`).** *"An inner Anglican debate"*; the receptionist reading *"little-o orthodox as acceptable"*; and — the part that is not merely irenic — *"I've actually defended it in debates I've done while not holding to it myself."* **The `RV-14` / `IP-25` / `IP-80` intellectual-honesty pattern in its strongest recorded form.**
- ⭐⭐ **Church authority affirmed and infallibility denied in the same breath, with his own submission stated first-person (`LS-86`).** Article XX taught: *"sola scriptura does not deny the authority of the church"*, *"as a Christian I am submitted to that authority"*, and *"nor is it a confession that the church is infallible"*, bounded by the Article's own *"contrary to God's word written"*. **An authority that binds without being infallible, under Scripture, is the Anglican and the Reformed account both** — and it is the middle term between `LS-24` (2021) and `LS-40`/`IP-77`.
- ⭐ **The Donatist error refused, and refused on the right ground (`LS-88`).** The minister's wickedness — extended by him to secret unbelief — *"does not hinder the validity of the sacraments"*, because *"it is God working the sacraments through us; we are not the ones who are empowering it."* **Common ground, and the anti-clerical form of it is the form a Reformed reader would want.**
- ⭐ **Self-examination located in the communicant, not in the priest (`LS-92`, this half only).** *"Scripture itself says that a man should examine himself… before receiving communion, not necessarily to be examined by the priest"* — 1 Corinthians 11 read as the Reformed tradition reads it, while he keeps a real pastoral responsibility alongside it. ⛔ **The credit is for this half only; the four-criterion admission list is a Known Gap 11 datum, not a credit.**

**SIX DECLINES, WITH REASONS — RECORDED BECAUSE A SWEEP THAT ONLY CREDITS IS NOT A SWEEP** (`BLOG-16` precedent).

- ⛔⛔ **`LS-84` (holding all the formularies is *"technically"* impossible) — DECLINED, and this is the decline that matters most this pass.** It is the batch's headline and it is a **`VP-1` datum on a live and unresolved pair**. **Filing it as common ground would quietly settle by filing what `DELTA: UNKNOWN` exists to keep open** — the `IP-40` reasoning, applied unchanged — and it would invite exactly the *"binding"*/*"subscription"* substitution the framing guard forbids.
- ⛔⛔ **`LS-75` / `LS-90` (Eucharistic adoration) — DECLINED, and NOT on their merits.** `LS-90`'s *"the point of the Eucharist is to receive"* is genuinely shared. ⛔ **But `LS-75` records him, in the same batch, saying he is *"not necessarily opposed"* and has done it himself; crediting the refusal alone would put a half-truth in the section that exists to be fair to him** — the `IP-72` reasoning, and here the two halves are in the same batch rather than in different eras.
- ⛔⛔ **`LS-93` (Article XXVIII's *"lifted up"* clause read narrowly) — DECLINED.** The reverent-consumption rule is common ground and the construction it sits inside is **the open Bucket A question** (`IP-73`). ⛔ **Crediting a construction that is itself the question would prejudge it** — the `IP-73` reasoning exactly.
- ⛔ **`LS-79` (re-sacrifice denied) — DECLINED and the decline is emphatic.** It is the **anti-Roman half** of a cluster whose other half is the retained oblation vocabulary in §9, and he affirms the heavenly offering in the same breath. **The `IP-38`/`IP-39`/`IP-43` rule, applied unchanged.**
- ⛔ **`LS-95` (the walls of Anglican diversity) — DECLINED.** The anti-Zwinglian and pro-baptismal-regeneration halves are shared with a Reformed reader; **the women's-ordination sentence and the whole passage's subject — who is inside the tent — are a live intra-Anglican dispute, and the `260807-1` ruling declined to characterise his women's-ordination material at all.** ⛔ Crediting the agreeable halves of that passage would misrepresent it.
- ⛔ **`LS-97` (tradition not jettisoned for want of a proof text) — DECLINED, on the guard rather than on the merits.** It carries this pass's heaviest inline `DQ-9` do-not-deploy guard, and **a guarded item swept into §15 looks available** — the `IP-35`/`IP-36` reasoning, applied unchanged.

### ⭐⭐ A101-2026-08-16 common ground (added 260829-3) — swept and folded in the SAME pass that logged the findings

**FIVE CREDITS.**

- ⭐⭐ **The formulary used as authority, not cited as decoration (`IP-71`).** Asked why the five *"commonly called"* sacraments are not sacraments of the Gospel, he answers out of the **Second Book of Homilies, Homily 9**, named by number and read at length — and makes it the load-bearing ground of the distinction rather than an ornament on an argument he had already made. **This is exactly what `DQ-1` complains he does not do, done.** ⛔ The complaint is narrowed, not answered: two Homilies out of thirty-three is not an account of how they bind.
- ⭐⭐ **Transubstantiation refused on a creational principle (`IP-74`).** *"Sacraments do not destroy God's good creation"* — God works in, with and through the created order rather than annihilating it. **Common ground with the Reformed position on the point at issue, and reached by a better argument than the bare appeal to the Article.**
- ⭐ **Article XXX kept without reservation, and against real pressure (`IP-79`).** The cup never withheld — *"even during COVID"*, when withholding would have been easy and defensible on public-health grounds. **A practice datum, and the strongest kind: conduct under a live incentive to do otherwise.**
- ⭐ **Article XXIV kept without reservation (`IP-83`).** The vernacular affirmed flatly, with the same commitment credited to the Eastern churches and to Rome today. ⛔ No lever here and none sought.
- ⭐ **The opposing case conceded before being answered (`IP-80`).** On polity he grants that the Presbyterian reading *"can make an argument… in Scripture"* before arguing the Episcopal one is *"equally as strong"* — the `IP-25`/`RV-14` intellectual-honesty pattern in current voice, and it recurs at `IP-75`, where he declines to make his own Article XXIX position a test of fellowship.

**SIX DECLINES, WITH REASONS — RECORDED BECAUSE A SWEEP THAT ONLY CREDITS IS NOT A SWEEP** (`BLOG-16` precedent).

- ⛔ **`IP-73` (the tabernacle and Article XXVIII) — DECLINED, and it is the decline that matters most this pass.** It is the session's sharpest **Bucket A** item: the Article lists *reserved* alongside *worshipped* and his reading makes the fourth verb govern the first three. ⛔ **Crediting a construction that is itself the open question would prejudge it.**
- ⛔ **`IP-72` (Eucharistic adoration refused) — DECLINED, and NOT on its merits.** The refusal is genuinely common ground with the Reformed position. ⛔ **But it cannot be credited apart from `IP-73`, which records him reserving the same day; crediting the refusal alone would put a half-truth in the section that exists to be fair to him.**
- ⛔ **`IP-70` (private confession) — DECLINED.** Whether a priest hearing private confession with the laying on of hands is common ground depends on the reader's tradition, and the finding's value is as a **Known Gap 11** datum, not as a credit.
- ⛔ **`IP-76` (baptismal regeneration decoupled from election) — DECLINED.** The Augustinian distinction is elegant and is genuinely his; ⛔ **but the position it makes coherent is one the Reformed reader disputes, and "he argues it well" is not the same as "he is sound here."**
- ⛔ **`IP-78` (paedocommunion) — DECLINED.** A live intra-Reformed dispute, not common ground, ⛔ and it sits in unaddressed tension with `IP-64`'s real-presence floor.
- ⛔ **`IP-82` (the five as ecclesial sacraments) — DECLINED.** The generous construction of Article XXV is a Bucket A item in miniature for the same reason as `IP-73`; ⛔ **not creditable while the construction is the thing in question.**

## 16. Ante-Nicene/Nicene Fathers Class — Content & Guest Lectures (2025)

**RJ's own teaching (sessions 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9):**

- Method laid out in §2 above (received religion; fathers as guide; consensus weighty but fallible; flag idiosyncrasy). **[Stated, ANF-1]**  
- Walks the standard ante-Nicene corpus with sound Protestant-historical instincts: the *Didache* (earliest catechism, "two ways"); *1 Clement* (apostolic succession as non-magical; notes Clement seems to teach **justification by faith alone**, ch. 32); *Epistle of Barnabas* (critiqued for **over-allegorizing** the OT — the food-law-as-"don't-associate-with-pig-people" reading — and for treating the OT as myth); Justin Martyr's *Dialogue with Trypho* and *Apologies* (Christ fulfills a *true* OT; real-presence-flavored Eucharist language; the "atheist" accusation explained). **[Stated, ANF-2,3,6]**  
- Names the two perennial errors he steers between: **Judaizing** (Ebionites) and **Gnosticizing** (Marcion) — wants OT and NT held together, ceremonies as fulfilled-in-Christ types. **[Stated, ANF-3]**  
- "Not quite saints" session (8): **Tertullian** praised for *trinitas* and rigor but faulted for (a) the heresy that grave post-baptismal sins can't be forgiven — which RJ ties to delayed-baptism distortions *and* to Rome's later penance system — (b) opposing infant baptism, (c) Montanism (proto-charismatic). **Origen** praised as a genius but faulted for subordinationism, pre-existence of souls, universal salvation (apokatastasis), and allegorical excess. Good Reformed-adjacent discernment throughout. **[Stated, ANF-8]**  
- Constantine session (9): debunks "Constantine invented Christianity/the Trinity/the canon" — stresses Constantine **died an Arian** (deathbed baptism); Edict of Milan = toleration, *not* establishment; Nicaea I convened to answer Arius; Arianism resurged *after* 325. Repeats the no-true-ecumenical-council-while-the-church-is-divided line and the bishops-from-the-apostles argument (Ignatius, Pastoral Epistles). **[Stated, ANF-9]**

**Guest lectures — attribute to the guest, not RJ:**

- **Dr. Stephen Boyce on Ignatius (ANF-4)** — a Baptist-trained scholar (doctorate, Louisiana Baptist) who converted toward this tradition. Pushes harder than RJ: argues Ignatius held **in persona Christi** ("to obey the bishop is to obey Christ"), a realist Eucharist ("the flesh of our Savior," vs. the Gnostics who "abstain"), martyrdom as sacrifice, and that venerating relics/saints follows. Closes with a strong "either the postapostolic church got the Eucharist/episcopate right universally, or we're all doomed" argument and a near-dismissal of the symbolic view. **RJ's response** was telling: he didn't amplify it — he posed the sola-scriptura-vs-consensus counter-question (see §2). **[Stated by Boyce, not RJ]**  
- **Tyler West on Hippolytus (ANF-7)** — a recent congregant, ex-Baptist. Uses the *Apostolic Tradition* to argue the parish's whole ceremonial (Gloria Patri, sponsors at baptism, infant baptism, threefold baptismal interrogation = Apostles' Creed, **baptismal regeneration**, the *Dominus vobiscum*, Eucharistic reverence/ablutions, fixed daily prayer hours, **the sign of the cross as a literal spiritual "shield" that deflects Satan**) descends from the apostles. This is the most ceremonially maximalist and most "the practices are spiritual warfare" content in the whole corpus — and it's **West's framing, not RJ's**. Useful as evidence of what RJ platforms, but do not quote it as RJ's doctrine. **[Stated by West, not RJ]**  
- **Kevin Valdez on Athanasius (ANF-5)** — sympathetic-to-Reformed in places (cites Presbyterian Bruce Gore; "theology matters"; mocks "relationship not religion" and "40,000 denominations"); solid Nicene history; nothing notably Romeward. The most Reformed-comfortable of the guests. **[Stated by Valdez]**

**[Analysis]** The guest line-up is itself a datum: RJ platforms ex-Baptist converts who frame the early church as proof the "symbol-only" view is a late deviation — i.e., his apologetic energy runs *toward* sacramental realism and *against* low-church memorialism. That's the direction of his project. But in his own voice he stays more measured than his guests, and he reserves the sola-scriptura check even while hosting them.

## 17. Christ in the OT Class — Hermeneutic & Covenant Theology (2025, all RJ)

- **Method: christotelic typology.** The OT is read as a unified story pointing forward to Christ — shadow→substance (Moses *foreshadows*, Christ *casts the shadow*); the whole arc is "the undoing of the fall," Genesis 3 → Revelation 22; redemption = the rewinding of fall/flood/Babel. Heavy on *fulfillment* language (37×) and *type/shadow*. Reads explicitly Christological types throughout: the protoevangelium (Gen 3:15), the flood-as-baptism (1 Pet 3:21, baptism the *greater* reality), Passover lamb/blood-on-doorposts → cross + Eucharist, the bronze serpent (John 3:14), Melchizedek's bread-and-wine → Eucharist (Heb 7), Moses as prophet-priest-king → Christ, Joshua (=Yeshua) leading into the land, David as shepherd/warrior/psalmist/king → Christ. **[Stated, COT-1 through COT-7]**  
- **Covenant theology, one people of God:** Gentiles grafted into the same tree (Rom 11); heirs of Abraham's promises via union with Christ the true "seed" (Gal 3); promised land → all creation in the resurrection. This is the engine of his anti-dispensationalism. **[Stated, COT-5]**  
- **Creation:** *creatio ex nihilo* defended against "God merely formed pre-existing matter"; ties it to classical theism and divine aseity. Genesis 1:26 read as a hint of the Trinity. **[Stated, COT-1]**  
- **Law/gospel + union with Christ:** the OT sacrificial system instills "blood atonement is necessary for forgiveness"; Christ the final, non-repeatable sacrifice (Heb), who "daily presents himself before the Father interceding" (note: this intercession-language recurs and is doing the same work as his Eucharistic "re-presentation, not re-sacrifice" line — §9/§10). Salvation = union with Christ, received in *word and sacrament*, not "mere declaration" — "already but not yet," simul iustus et peccator. Reformed-adjacent, with the sacramental-realist accent. **[Stated, COT-4, COT-5, COT-6]**  
- **Eucharistic readings of the OT (relevant to the presence question):** the showbread, the Passover lamb (eaten), the grain/"meat" offering, and Melchizedek's bread-and-wine are all read as foreshadowing Holy Communion, in which "we receive the body and blood of Christ" — reinforcing his realist (not memorialist) presence view from a typological angle, while still denying re-sacrifice. **[Stated, COT-3, COT-5, COT-6, COT-7]**  
- **A datum about his circle (COT-6):** he mentions a "priest friend" who holds that the OT religion was a "paganized" capitulation to surrounding paganism — RJ explicitly *rejects* this (God Himself laid out the sacrificial system; it's not a concession to paganism). Tells you he's actively debating these questions with at least one other clergyman and stakes out the conservative side.  
- **[Analysis]** The hermeneutic is solidly within Reformed-covenantal bounds and is mostly *common ground* with you — which is itself useful: it means the incense tension (§13) and the presence question (§8) can be argued on *shared* typological premises rather than across a hermeneutical gulf. The one cross-tradition friction is the atonement-emphasis point (§5).


- **★ THE FULLEST CONTINUITY STATEMENT HE HAS GIVEN: one tree, expansion not recreation (RV-12).** *"It should be noted that Israel and the church are a continuity and an expansion, not a disruption or a recreation."* And: *"The family of God has never changed in It's never been from one tree to another a different tree."* Developed at length via Romans 11, with both dispensational bifurcation and replacement theology explicitly rejected ("This is a big no-no"). **[Stated, RV-12]**
  - ⚠️ **[Analysis], and the distinction is the whole point:** this is a stated continuity of the **PEOPLE** of God, argued from Romans 11 and from the ingrafting of the Gentiles. **He says nothing here about continuity of WORSHIP PRACTICE**, and the step from the one to the other is **exactly the step DQ-5 was asking him to make explicit**. ⚠️ **Do not log this as an answer to the OT-filter question and do not let it be summarised as one.** Its value is that it puts his continuity premise on record **in his own words**, so that the filter question can be asked against a *stated* premise rather than an *assumed* one. Cross-ref DQ-5, DQ-8, DQ-9.

## 18. Revelation Class — Eschatology, Hermeneutic & the Heavenly-Worship Hinge ⛔ *(**heading corrected 260822-2: read "the 2026 series — early batch `Rev`, Sessions I-VIII; tracked batch `RV`, Sessions IX-XI, XIII, XIV." THERE IS NO 2025 RUN AND NO 2026 RUN; THERE IS ONE SERIES.** Original heading text retained below per the never-alter rule.)* (2025 run, `Rev`, all RJ; **2026 run, sessions IX-XI, XIII and XIV, `RV`, below** — ⚠️ *"IX-XI" corrected to "IX-XI and XIII" 260814-1 with the Session XIII ingest, and extended to "IX-XI, XIII and XIV" 260815-1 with the Session XIV ingest; the heading's own text up to "Hinge" is unchanged in both passes, because `BLOG-93` anchors on it*)

8 sessions, all taught by RJ (no guests this batch). Covers the intro/three millennial views and four timeline approaches (session 1); chapters 1–3, the Son-of-Man vision and seven churches (session 2); chapter 4, the heavenly throne-room worship (session 3); chapter 5 + start of 6, the Lamb and the seals (session 4); chapter 7, the 144,000 and the great multitude (session 5); chapter 8, the seventh seal and first four trumpets (session 6); chapter 9, the fifth/sixth trumpets and the binding of Satan (session 7); chapter 10, the mighty angel and the eating of the scroll (session 8). Tagged Rev-1…Rev-8 by session.

**Eschatology & interpretive frame:**

- **Postmillennial + partial preterist** (see §5 for the doctrinal summary). Most of Revelation fulfilled by ~AD 70; the temple's destruction is the great covenantal hinge (the earthly temple judged; the church revealed as the true temple; Heb 8:13 "the first is obsolete"). Dates Revelation to the 60s / pre-AD 70 (Neronian), which is load-bearing for the preterism. Presents pre-/a-/post-millennial as all orthodox and explicitly non-dogmatized in his jurisdiction; rejects **hyper-preterism** (denies the creeds and bodily resurrection). **[Stated, Rev-1, Rev-4, Rev-8]**  
- **Anti-dispensationalism + even-handed rejection of its antisemitic backlash.** Restates "fulfillment theology" (one people of God, not "replacement theology"; Gal + Rom 9–11) — *and* explicitly rejects the modern reactive error in the opposite direction (treating ethnic Jews as beyond redemption), naming it as an obsession he's encountered (flags a debate where someone "randomly brings up… the Jews" and treats questioning interracial marriage as "a red flag"). The modern state of Israel has no direct end-times role except possibly as a gathering-point for a future mass conversion of Jews (Rom 11:25–26, an "early church interpretation," held by Irenaeus). **[Stated, Rev-1, Rev-5, Rev-8]**  
- **Genre-sensitive hermeneutic: anti-wooden-literalist, anti-"spiritualizing-away."** Apocalyptic imagery is hyperbolic/cosmic ("earth-shattering"; "raining cats and dogs"), to be read by the interpretation Scripture itself supplies — against both the "Apache helicopters" dispensational literalism he was raised in *and* against gutting plain statements like "I and the Father are one." Cosmic-collapse language (sun/moon/stars) = the fall of world-orders (Isa 13, Ezek 32, Joel 2 applied to Babylon/Egypt/Judah), not literal astronomy. Insists on exegesis over isogesis and on reading in historical-cultural context (see §2, Rev-3/Rev-6). **[Stated, Rev-1, Rev-6]**  
- **High Christology, explicitly anti-unitarian.** Notes he is currently debating "people who deny the deity of Christ" and finds Revelation strong evidence (Father and Lamb jointly worshipped; the Lamb takes the scroll from the Father's hand = ontological equality; dyothelite handling of "the Father is greater than I" = *secundum humanitatem*). Son-of-Man vision (Rev 1) read robustly: golden sash = priesthood, white hair = eternity/wisdom, two-edged sword = the conquering gospel. **[Stated, Rev-2, Rev-4]**  
- **Keys / Matt 16:18 again (Rev 3:7, Philadelphia):** keys held by Christ, delegated to *all* apostles (Matt 18:18), not Peter alone; claims Rome itself concedes this at "Lateran I, canon 1." Consistent with §2/A101-V. **[Stated, Rev-2; the Lateran citation is Clarify — verify it actually says this]**  
- **Seven churches read pastorally, NOT as a church-age timeline** — explicitly debunks the dispensational "seven ages" scheme he was raised on. Notable pastoral note (Pergamum): work to maintain unity and reclaim the erring *before* excommunication; heresy doesn't instantly un-church. **[Stated, Rev-2]**  
- **Binding of Satan already accomplished (~AD 70)** on his postmil/preterist reading — Satan "bound" (the mafia-kingpin-in-jail analogy: operation continues but without unified command), demonic power "diminished" though real. **[Stated, Rev-7]**

**🎯 The heavenly-worship hinge (the reason this batch was commissioned):**

- **RJ explicitly derives earthly incense AND an earthly altar from Revelation's heavenly worship — stated flatly and repeatedly.** This is the core yield. On Rev 8:3–5 (the angel with the golden censer at the golden altar): *"not only is incense being used, but an altar as well. **Again, we take a lot of our worship theology from the book of Revelation. This is one of the reasons we have incense. This is one of the reasons why we have an altar.**"* Stacking Exod 30:1–10 + Luke 1:8–10 + Mal 1:11: *"a central aspect of worship, both the incense and the altar. **And that's how it is for us. We have both as part of our worship, as the standard part of our worship.**"* On Rev 5:8 (the bowls of incense = the prayers of the saints): *"Psalm 141:2… we see that all throughout the Old Testament, **which is why we use incense at church.**"* **[Stated, Rev-9 (= Rev session 6, the altar/censer passage), Rev-10 (= Rev session 4, the bowls passage)]**  
- **The governing principle behind it: heavenly-pattern participation.** Threaded through the class — earthly worship *participates in / patterns itself on* the heavenly worship John sees. On the Sanctus (Rev 4:8) → the Sursum Corda: *"we are joining in the heavenly worship with the angels and archangels and with all the hosts of heaven… we get that from Revelation 4,"* present "in just about every liturgy, east or west, the earliest ones." On Rev 5: *"this isn't reflecting our worship. **Our worship is reflecting their worship.**"* On Rev 7: *"our worldview should be first and foremost informed by our worship."* **[Stated, Rev-11 (= the heavenly-participation principle, stated across Rev sessions 3–5)]**  
- **He reads the heavenly incense itself as a *symbol*.** Rev 5:8 and 8:3–4 *interpret* the bowls/smoke as "the prayers of the saints," and he affirms "incense is all throughout scripture symbolic of prayer" (Ps 141:2). The angel-priest at the altar he plausibly identifies as **Christ** in his priestly/intercessory role (Heb). So the vision, on his own reading, signifies *the prayers of the saints + Christ's heavenly intercession* — the fulfilled realities, not a mandate for sanctuary furniture. **[Stated, Rev-9, Rev-10]**  
- **Tag-mapping note:** to keep the source line clean, **Rev-9** = the altar/incense statements (Rev 8 passage, taught in Rev session 6); **Rev-10** = the bowls-of-incense statement (Rev 5 passage, taught in Rev session 4); **Rev-11** = the heavenly-pattern-participation principle (stated across the chapter 4–7 sessions). The session numbers and the finding numbers don't line up one-to-one because the hinge material is what got pulled out and numbered for the question list; the plain session tags (Rev-1…Rev-8) cover everything else.

**Other reinforcements (cross-referenced, not re-derived):**

- **Word + sacrament realism (Rev 10, eating the scroll):** the sweet-then-bitter scroll explicitly mapped onto "the two ways in the liturgy that we receive Christ — in word and in sacrament." Reinforces §17 / COT word-and-sacrament union. **[Stated, Rev-8]**  
    
- **Apostasy/perseverance (Rev 5/7):** restates COT-2 — willful "belligerent apostasizing" = being cut off (Rom 11; Heb 6/10; 1 John 2:19), distinct from stumbling; anti-synergism guard on Phil 2:12–13. See §7. **[Stated, Rev-5, Rev-8]**  
    
- **Sola scriptura in operation (Rev 3/8):** refuses to dogmatize the four-creatures-as-Gospels reading beyond scriptural warrant; rejects presuppositionless biblicism. See §2. **[Stated, Rev-3, Rev-6]**  
    
- **Image/2nd-commandment: silent.** The class says nothing about images, statues, icons, the 2nd commandment, or Nicaea II — a notable negative finding given the subject matter. One adjacent *descriptive* remark about early-church relic/martyr veneration (Rev 7) is **not** an endorsement. See §12. **[Stated (descriptive), Rev-5]**  
    
- **[Analysis]** This batch is the most consequential since Batch 2 for one reason: it converts OQ8 from a strong inference into a documented, repeated, in-his-own-voice practice-rationale — *and* it surfaces the exact counter-argument (heavenly-pattern participation) he will deploy, so the question can be built to survive it. Everything else in the class is either Reformed-friendly (postmil/preterism, anti-dispensationalism, high Christology, word-and-sacrament, exegesis-not-isogesis) or a re-confirmation of priors (apostasy/FV proximity, keys). No contradictions with any prior batch. The incense/altar finding is, as before, an internal *tension within RJ* (his apocalyptic-symbolic and Hebrews-fulfillment hermeneutics vs. his literalized heavenly furniture), not a contradiction between batches.

### The 2026 run — sessions IX-XI (RV batch, added 260725-4)

*⚠️ **A different run of the same class.** The `Rev` findings above are the 2025 series; `RV` is the 2026 series, sessions IX onward. **Do not merge the two tag series** (`PROJECT_STATE.md` §5 rule 7). **🎯 The hermeneutics fork — the highest-value item in the batch, and it cuts in a direction that needs DECIDING, not assuming.**

- **★★ The imagery-and-symbolism principle appears here as a rule of INTERPRETATION, not of worship (RV-2).** *"we we recognize that scripture is replete with imagery, with symbolism. And so, what we do is we say, 'What are these signs and symbols and images pointing to?' They're pointing to a deeper reality."* **[Stated, RV-2]** This is **DQ-9's vocabulary almost exactly** — signs, symbols and images pointing past themselves to a deeper reality — **doing interpretive work rather than liturgical work.**
  - **[Analysis] TWO READINGS, BOTH LIVE, NEITHER CHOSEN:**
  - **(a) One principle, two registers.** The DQ-9 formulation ("imagery and symbolism are to reflect the Biblical witness") and this are **the same commitment about how symbol works**, applied once to text and once to liturgy. On this reading **DQ-9 is load-bearing theology and must be met on its own ground.**
  - **(b) A hermeneutical maxim under strain.** This is **a rule for reading apocalyptic that has been carried across into a question about warrant for acts**, where it does different work. On this reading DQ-9's "principle" is a **category transfer**, and the reply is to ask what the principle is a principle *of*.
  - ⚠️ **DO NOT FOLD THIS INTO EITHER READING IN THE CORPUS. THE DISTINCTION IS THE FINDING.**
  - ⚠️ **[Analysis] — and this is the PROJECT'S argument, not his:** on his own statement here, an image *points past itself* to a deeper reality. Applied to Revelation 5:8 and 8:3-4, that pressure runs toward the incense imagery **signifying prayer rather than mandating material incense**, and Revelation 5:8 glosses itself in exactly that direction. **He does not say this and must never be quoted as saying it.**
- **★ Multiple simultaneous true interpretations, stated against dispensationalism (RV-11).** *"The ones that are more dispensational will tend to refuse to ever believe that there are layers to the inter- interpretations of scripture,"* and *"there there can very often be multiple interpretations that happen and all of them be true."* **[Stated, RV-11]** **[Analysis]** This is **the same move as RV-2 at one further remove, and it SHARPENS the RV-2 fork rather than resolving it.** Under reading **(a)** his tolerance for layered meaning is a general commitment that would also loosen act-level specificity in worship. Under reading **(b)** it is a claim about *texts* having more than one true referent, which has **no obvious carry into what may be DONE**. **Logged as sharpening RV-2, not as a finding against him.**

## Cross-Batch Reconciliation (where Batch 2 and the merge note needed correcting)

1. **"Body, blood, soul, divinity" — the merge note flagged this as Tridentine concomitance language he's personally pressing (and tied it to withholding the cup).** Source check: RJ uses the phrase to describe the *shared catholic overlap* (Rome/Lutheran/Anglican/Reformed), then immediately denies *local* presence (Aquinas), calls the remaining differences "philosophical," and settles on "in receiving the bread and the wine we are receiving the body and blood of Christ." And he is *against* withholding the cup. So the internal-tension lever is weaker than the note implies — it's a fair question, not a "gotcha." Article **29** (the wicked "in no wise are partakers of Christ") remains a genuine and citable lever against his stated **Lutheran lean**, and that one holds up.  
     
2. **"Reverencing the altar enacts adoration of the host."** Source check: he explicitly frames it as respecting sacred *space* (Ark analogy), explicitly *not* "prostrating in an idolatrous way," and even notes the OT was "almost iconoclastic." The Article 28 tension (reservation/elevation) is real, but his reverence rationale is space-and-presence, not host-as-object adoration. Press it as a question about whether the *practices* outrun the *stated theology*, not as a claim that he adores the host.  
     
3. **"He uses icons; bows at the name of Jesus; distinguishes veneration of saints from worship (dulia/latria); refers to the Blessed Virgin" — merge note billed this as "fresh ammunition" for the Nicaea II / Art. 22 question.** Source check tempers it: the veneration language is about *living heroes / historical figures* as an analogy, not saints or images; dulia/latria are **not** used; "icons" appears only in passing in the five-senses list; "Blessed Virgin" is a one-off descriptive reference to the Magnificat. So Batch 2 confirms icons/vestments are physically present and that he reasons honor ≠ worship for human figures — but it does **not** show him defending icon veneration, invoking saints, or engaging Nicaea II. The unskippable question from Batch 1 stays unskippable; Batch 2 gives context but not the smoking gun the note suggested.  
     
4. **Perkins anachronism (merge note's #2 opening).** This holds up and is worth keeping: RJ leans on Perkins (a thoroughgoing Calvinist Puritan, *A Reformed Catholike* 1597) for both his "reformed catholic" identity *and*, by adjacency, his ceremonial program. Perkins's "reformed catholicity" was *doctrinal* (we hold the catholic faith, Rome corrupts it), not a license for vestments/incense/reservation. Clean, friendly seam — but frame it as "Perkins would be surprised by the ceremonial," not "you've misread Perkins on doctrine."  
     
5. **Consistency with Batch 1:** no contradictions between the batches. Batch 2 deepens, doesn't reverse: the sola fide / imputation / simul iustus from A101 reappears (AW); the transubstantiation rejection and two-acceptable-presence-views reappear (now with the explicit Lutheran lean stated more strongly); baptismal regeneration reappears; the "Marxist infiltration / left TEC" narrative reappears. The one genuinely *new* doctrinal datum is the **strength** of his Lutheran-presence lean and the **ceremonial maximalism** (reservation, elevation, holy water, tabernacle) that A101 didn't surface.  
     
6. **Revelation batch (2025) — consistent, and it resolves OQ8's evidentiary status.** No contradictions with any prior batch. It *confirms* priors (anti-dispensationalism/one-people-of-God from COT; apostasy/FV-proximity from COT-2; the sola-scriptura *norma normata* posture from §2; word-and-sacrament realism from §17) and adds genuinely new, Reformed-friendly data (postmillennialism + partial preterism; high anti-unitarian Christology). The **one finding that changes the corpus** is on the incense/altar hinge: what was an *inference* in Batch 2 (he leans on Rev 8 / Mal 1:11 for incense) is now an explicit, repeated, in-his-own-voice statement — *"this is one of the reasons we have incense… one of the reasons we have an altar… as the standard part of our worship."* That **strengthens** OQ8. The one *complication* it introduces is the **heavenly-pattern-participation** warrant ("our worship is reflecting their worship"), which is a second, distinct rationale not reducible to OT-revival and not obviously caught by the COT fulfillment rule — so the sharpest form of the question had to be re-aimed at the seam between his two warrants (§13, OQ8). Net: the Revelation batch is the strongest single confirmation of the central lever in the whole project, with the bonus that it pre-discloses his likely defense.  
     
7. **One correction applied throughout v0.6 (not a batch reconciliation, but logged here for traceability):** earlier drafts framed JD's vantage point as "Reformed Baptist / ~LBCF 1689." Corrected to JD's actual position — **classically Reformed Presbyterian (PCA/OPC, broadly WCF)**, covenant theology (moderate on dispensationalism), open to the LBCF-1689 view of baptismal *mode/subjects*, supportive of the 39 Articles *except* the extended fasting seasons (Lent regarded as a 4th-c. ascetical accretion), largely strict on the RPW but not on Sabbath-recreation or exclusive psalmody, firmly opposed to incense and other normative-principle practices. The substantive consequence is in §7: the baptism disagreement is **regeneration/objectivity (FV proximity), not the mode of baptism** — keep the pressure off paedo- vs. credo-baptism. See the "My own position" note at the top.

8. **RC batch (Roman Catholicism set, RC-1…RC-7), fills the papacy gap, develops several findings over time, no contradictions with prior batches.** The RC set spans RJ's own widest timeline (deacon-era 2020-21 through 2025), so its primary reconciliation work is *internal*, tracking his own development, rather than correcting a prior merge note. Four specific reconciliations:
   - **Episcopacy:** RC1-3 (essence/fullness language, 2020-2021) sits against IP-10 (bene esse, not esse, 2026). Possible genuine development across a six-year span from deacon to rector; re-opens (without resolving) whether the apostolic-succession down-weight in D5 still holds at full strength. See QC-c.
   - **Incense warrant:** RC3-10 (Malachi decisive, "the final nail in the coffin," 2025) sits against IP-1/IP-3 (Malachi demoted to one supporting prong inside the heaven-earth-participation structure, 2026). Development confirmed in his own retrospective comment ("not so insistent" when first ordained).
   - **Eucharistic lean:** RC-3 (2025, holds both Lutheran and Calvinist emphases simultaneously, explicitly non-local high presence) sits against the circa-2020 "Barely Protestant" finding ("between Luther and Calvin, sometimes leaning more towards Calvin") and the class corpus's "leans firmly Lutheran" (§8). He holds both emphases in the Anglican dual formula; the "lean" he reports varies by occasion rather than being fixed; see §8 cross-batch note above.
   - **Homilies:** RC1-10 (disagrees with "certain Homilies," unspecified, 2020-2021) sits against the later IP-era note that he "affirmed the Homilies but hedged self-contradiction." Possible development, or a stable general-affirmation-with-unspecified-exceptions position held across both periods. See QC-b.
   
   No batch-to-batch contradictions otherwise: the RC set confirms sola fide (RC1-15), baptismal regeneration (RC1-4), real presence and anti-transubstantiation (RC1-3/4), and the anti-Puritan ceremonial instinct (RC1-11) were all present from the deacon era onward, not later accretions, useful to know when assessing whether any given Bucket A lever is pressing a recent drift or a stable, long-held position.

9. **BP batch ("Barely Protestant" YouTube channel, 5 videos), BP-internal + BP-vs-RC dating cross-check.** The BP batch's internal date-spread (2020 videos vs. the current-era BP-RPW livestream) independently corroborates the established pattern (item 8, above) of reading divergences across this corpus developmentally rather than as contradictions. Specific instances this batch adds to that timeline: icon use moves from a 2020 affirmative-defense register (BP-Icons) toward the more cautious "not required, could be idolatry" register of ANF-1 (2024-25) and the confirmed-but-restrained RC3-12 (2025) — consistent in substance (never requires veneration) but shifting in emphasis. The Malachi/heaven-participation incense-warrant balance does NOT move in one direction across this span — BP-RPW (current-era) restates Malachi with full imperatival weight, against the IP-2/RC3-10 "Malachi demoted" reading drawn from teaching contexts — suggesting the warrant's foregrounding may be register-dependent (teaching vs. polemical/informal) rather than a clean one-way historical shift. See §13's BP-39 entry for the recommended revision to the existing reweight note.

## Open Questions & Known Tensions (feeder for the question list)

1. **Nicaea II / icons — substantially resolved, now refined.** RJ does not require icon veneration and grants it could be seen as idolatry (§3). The remaining question is narrow: *would he defend veneration as a legitimate option, or only decline to impose it?* And the sharper follow-up: *if the Seventh Council anathematizes non-venerators and you don't bind it, in what sense is it "ecumenical" for you — and who decides which conciliar canons bind?* That last is the friendly sola-scriptura lever, now grounded in his own words.  
2. **Icon — and statue — practice specifically** — the parish has icons (confirmed, and icon *use* now directly sourced, RC3-12) and carved apostle statues (JD report). Are any venerated by him or the congregation (bowed to, kissed, censed, candles/flowers before them, feast-day honor), or decorative/didactic? He's said veneration isn't *required*; observed practice would tell you whether it's *present*. (Statues get their own fuller treatment in OQ13 and §12.)  
3. **Invocation of saints** — still only inferred "no." Confirm, and distinguish prayer *to* saints vs. calendar honor vs. "ora pro nobis."  
4. **Marian doctrines** — Theotokos certain (Ephesus, now independently sourced RC6-1); Assumption / Immaculate Conception as pious opinions (IC's usual prooftext now doubted by RJ himself, RC4-5)? Perpetual virginity?

   - ⭐ **UPDATE 260809-1 (`A101-2026-07-26`): THE IC SUB-QUESTION GETS ITS FIRST CURRENT-VOICE DATUM (`IP-32`, `[S]`-sourced).** Teaching Article XV: only Christ is without sin, *"and this includes the blessed virgin"* — she *"committed actual sins"*; an Anglo-Catholic friend's IC belief described as a position *"some"* Anglicans hold, against *"our formularies."* **The IC line: 2016 cannot-hold → 2019 flat denial → 2025 prooftext doubted → 2026 taught-from-Article-XV.** ⛔ **The Assumption sub-question and `VP-7` are UNTOUCHED (different Marian questions, fenced at `VP-7`); perpetual virginity and invocation unchanged; one `[S]` clause in the stretch is garbled and quoted by nobody (see `IP-32`).**  
5. **Article 28 vs. reservation/elevation, UN-GATED.** Both elevation (RC3-18/23) and reservation (RC3-27) are now independently sourced from his own 2025 Mass-teaching, in addition to the Recon-Euch material, internal and citable, with the caveat in §10/Cross-Batch note 2 that his reverence rationale is space-and-presence, not host-as-object adoration. The one sub-prong still open: whether he specifically *adores* the reserved sacrament (vs. reserving it only for the sick); see QC-d.  
6. **Article 29 vs. his Lutheran presence-lean** — the cleanest internal lever from Batch 2; Art. 29 sides Reformed against the view he prefers, though see the §8 cross-batch note that the "lean" varies by source/date. **Hardened (GV batch):** the Lutheran/corporeal lean is now triangulated and sourced (GV-15/16/21/36/46/51), and his title-vs-content deflection on Art. 29 is itself sourced (GV-43) and pre-empted by anchoring on Art. 29's *content*; the lever is now CONTENT-anchored (QA-Euc), not lean-dependent.  
7. **Element/circumstance (WCF 1.6)** — he's only refuted the populist RPW; the confessional one distinguishes elements (warrant) from circumstances (prudence), which his examples blur.  
8. 🎯 **His own fulfillment hermeneutic vs. his incense/altar practice (COT-3/6 + Rev-9/10/11 vs AW-I) — the strongest internal lever in the corpus, now documented and sharpened.**
   - ✅⭐⭐ **THE LEVER NOW RESTS ON VERIFIED GROUND (260813-1) — AND UNTIL THIS PASS IT DID NOT.** `Rev-9/10/11 (2025)` had **no registered source of any kind** from ingest until 260813-1: no file, no hash, no offsets. **The source is now registered (Files 8-9) and every load-bearing quotation is located byte-exact:** *"not only is incense being used, but an altar as well"* → **File 9 @45,995**; *"one of the reasons we have incense" / "one of the reasons why we have an altar"* → **@46,123 / @46,167**; *"which is why we use incense at church"* → **File 8 @93,657**. **All three legs of the threefold rationale — (a), (b), (c) below — are verified**, as is the Exod 30 / Luke 1 / Mal 1:11 stack behind (a) and (b). ⚠️ **TWO CARRY-FORWARD CAUTIONS, both about WORDING and neither about substance:** (i) the *"standard part of our worship"* sentence was **silently disfluency-cleaned** when the batch was written and **does not grep in the corpus's form** (`Rev-9a` — use the ASR wording in any `FIND:`); (ii) one `Rev-11` heavenly-participation quotation is a **compression presented as verbatim** and ⛔ **must not be put to him in the form the corpus holds it** (`Rev-11a`). ⛔ **The argument is undamaged; the quotation discipline is what needs care.** ⛔ **And this remains 2025 material — it is NOT his current position** (§5 rule 7; the 2026 `RV` run is separate). *(Full table in §18's retro-verification block.)* The Revelation class makes the practice-rationale *explicit and repeated*: "this is one of the reasons we have incense… one of the reasons we have an altar… as the standard part of our worship" (Rev 8); "which is why we use incense at church" (Rev 5). So three sub-levers, in ascending force (full development in §13):  
   - ⭐⭐ **UPDATE 260814-1 (Revelation Session XIII, 2026) — THE COMMISSIONED TEST WAS RUN ON THE CHAPTER MOST LIKELY TO MOVE THIS LEVER, AND ⛔ THE LEVER DOES NOT MOVE IN EITHER DIRECTION.** **Revelation 15:8 fills the heavenly temple with smoke from the glory of God**, which is the imagery `Rev-9 (2025)` runs on; **Session XIII teaches that verse in current voice.** ⛔⛔ **`incense` IS 0 ACROSS ALL 28,532 BYTES. He reads the smoke as THEOPHANY — Sinai and Isaiah — and draws DIVINE INACCESSIBILITY from it, connecting it to no earthly practice whatever** (`RV-27 (2026)`). ⛔⛔ **STATED AS A HARD LIMIT BECAUSE IT IS THE SENTENCE MOST LIKELY TO BE OVER-READ IN EITHER DIRECTION: this is not a retraction, not a concession, and not evidence about what he would say if asked. It is one session in which the connection was available and was not made.** ⚠️ **A silence is not a position** (§5 rule 3). ⛔ **Sub-levers (a), (b) and (c) are exactly as they stood; nothing is added to them and nothing is subtracted.** ⭐⭐ **AND ONE GENUINE GAIN, WHICH IS ABOUT SUB-LEVER (a)'s PREMISE RATHER THAN ITS CONCLUSION:** `RV-31 (2026)` states the **temple's fulfilment** in current voice — the presence relocated *"in Christ"* and then carried by the church, which is *"God's visible temple."* ⛔⛔ **HE DRAWS NO CONSEQUENCE FOR FURNITURE, VESSELS OR CEREMONIAL. The step from fulfilment to non-reproduction is the PROJECT'S and he does not take it.** ⛔ **Do not take it for him.** ⚠️⚠️ **AND THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT GOT STRONGER, WHICH IS THE HONEST HALF OF THIS UPDATE:** `RV-28 (2026)` shows the **heavenly-worship vantage point** (`RV-3 (2026)`) recurring **four times in one session** and framing the whole chapter — so *"our worship is reflecting their worship"* is not an isolated 2025 remark but a habitual frame. ⛔ **He still draws no liturgical inference from it, and `Rev-11 (2025)` and `RV-28 (2026)` are DIFFERENT RUNS and must not be merged** (§5 rules 7 and 12).
   - **(a) Fulfillment (the original COT lever, restated to survive his escape hatch):** Hebrews forbids reviving fulfilled OT ceremonial because it implies Christ hasn't come; he typologizes the tabernacle altar of incense as a fulfilled shadow of "the prayers of the saints" and Christ's intercession — and Rev 8, on his own reading, *confirms* that the heavenly reality is intercession/prayer (the angel-priest plausibly Christ). So the vision points to the fulfilled reality; reproducing the shadow's physical apparatus is the move his Hebrews argument forbids.  
   - **(b) Apocalyptic genre (his own anti-literalist hermeneutic):** he reads the sea of glass, the living creatures, the 24 elders, the slain Lamb, the bowls as *symbols*, refusing to literalize them — so why is the incense the one piece of heavenly furniture reproduced as a literal physical object on earth? The selectivity is the tension.

RJ's teaching corpus is heavy on worship, sacraments, councils, OT typology, and Revelation; whole regions of his system go unmapped. These are the highest-value gaps — where a PCA/OPC reader has a definite position, the videos don't settle his, and real difference is plausible. Full question wording lives in the question list (Bucket D). Ordered by payoff. Several escalate from **[Clarify]** into **[by your own standard]** levers depending on his answer.

Two items previously flagged elsewhere as inferred-not-sourced are also now resolved: **elevation and reservation** (§10, §13/§Vestments, both confirmed via RC3-18/23 and RC3-27, no longer inferred) and **icon use** (§12, confirmed via RC3-12; icon *veneration* specifically remains open). 1. **"Old Catholic" self-identification + where justification falls. [Clarify → potential strongest A-lever]** He reportedly said he'd be comfortable being "Old Catholic" (JD field note, intro videos). Factual anchor: the **Union of Utrecht** rejected Vatican I (papal infallibility / universal jurisdiction), appeals to the undivided church of the first seven councils, keeps episcopacy + seven sacraments + apostolic succession, rejects the Marian dogmas and a *dogmatic* purgatory, and is in communion with Anglicans (Bonn Agreement, 1931). Crucially it is **not** "Trent minus the pope" — the mainstream German/Swiss branch *rejected Trent's authority* — and it never adopted sola fide or imputation. So comfort in that frame raises the deepest question in the project: does RJ treat **justification by faith alone** (Art. 11, "a most wholesome Doctrine," endorsing the *Homily of Salvation* by name) as *the* material issue of the Reformation, or as second-order? If the latter, this escalates into a Bucket A lever. His "fullness" language cuts both ways: a Protestant locates the fullness in the gospel rightly grasped, not in catholic order. **[JD note]**

## In-Person Findings (IP ledger — consolidated from the patch queue)

*Source: IP = in-person class + Q&A. IP-2 … IP-12 from the session dated 2026-06-14 (logged 2026-06-15). **IP-1.** [Stated] Anchor: §13 / OQ8 (incense warrant) — THE EARLIER MALACHI DATUM. Malachi 1:11 ("in every place incense shall be offered unto my name") stated as RJ's original PRIMARY incense prooftext, predating the 2026-06-14 session. Superseded in weight, not withdrawn, by IP-3's two-part heaven-earth-participation / OT-continuity structure, where it now functions as one supporting prong rather than the lead — see IP-3 and line 770 below. No independent quote/session anchor beyond the incense cluster's own record; promoted to a ledger entry per the do-only-if-cheap patch queue item (260727-1), pointing at its anchor rather than restating IP-3's content.

**IP-2.** [Stated] + [Analysis — for JD] Anchor: §13 / OQ8 (RPW seam) RJ explicitly self-identifies with the REGULATIVE principle ("rightly understood"), and explicitly REJECTS the normative-principle label as "too loosey-goosey" ("The normative principle generally is like unless Scripture forbids it, you can do it"). His stated RPW = "we want to reject what Scripture rejects… only worship the way Scripture says we can worship." [Analysis] The rule he actually OPERATES, however, is the conservative-reformation default he gave in the lecture: "keep something we have received in the tradition of the Church, unless there is a positive argument from Scripture or the consensus of the Church to reject it." That is functionally the NORMATIVE principle wearing RPW vocabulary — and it is the principle Art. 34 assumes ("every particular or national Church hath authority to ordain, change, and abolish ceremonies… ordained only by man's authority"). Internal-Anglican lever: classic Anglican worship-theology (Hooker; Art. 34) is normative, not regulative; his RPW claim is both historically contestable for Anglicanism and internally inconsistent with his own operative rule. — added 2026-06-15, from IP session 2026-06-14.

**IP-3.** [Stated] ★ (top lever) Anchor: §13 / OQ8 ; cross-ref IP-1, Rev-findings REWEIGHT OF INCENSE WARRANT. RJ's stated PRIMARY warrant has shifted from the Malachi 1:11 prooftext (IP-1) to a two-part structure he leads with: (a) HEAVEN-EARTH PARTICIPATION — "look at the Revelation worship. The Revelation worship is perfect worship… a heavenly vision of worship. It has incense. It has white robes. It has people around an altar, around the throne of God"; "in worship, there is actually a union of heaven and earth. That's part of what our theology is." (b) OT-CONTINUITY — only the bloody/animal SACRIFICIAL system is abrogated, because it pointed to Christ's one sacrifice; non-sacrificial ceremonial survives: "That is not an argument that incense is bad, or that vestments are bad, or that altars are bad… Only insofar as it is rejecting Christ's one sacrifice would it be bad." Malachi 1:11 (IP-1) now functions as ONE prong inside this structure, not the lead. SIGNIFICANCE: (b) is RJ's direct ANSWER to the OQ8/§13 fulfillment-seam. He pre-empts the Hebrews lever by distinguishing *sacrificial* ceremonial (fulfilled/abrogated) from *non-sacrificial* furniture (incense, altar, vestments — retained). CHARITABLE FLAG: this is a serious, non-trivial distinction JD must answer, NOT dismiss. He DEFENDS incense as expected/required, not merely permitted. — added 2026-06-15, from IP session 2026-06-14.

**IP-4.** [Stated] + [Analysis — for JD] Anchor: new sacraments section / SS-adjacent RJ affirms the FIVE "ecclesiastical" sacraments (confirmation, penance, orders, matrimony, unction) as GENUINE sacraments — "sacraments of the church," distinct in type from the two "dominical" sacraments but not denied the name. He claims Art. 25 "is not denying that the other five are sacraments… we don't want to reject their historic understanding of being sacraments." [Analysis] Internal-Anglican tension: Art. 25 states the five "are not to be counted for Sacraments of the Gospel… [and] have not like nature of Sacraments with Baptism, and the Lord's Supper." RJ's reading ("different type, but still sacraments") is contestable and leans into a seven-sacrament frame fenced by the dominical/ecclesiastical distinction. Clean internal lever. — added 2026-06-15, from IP session 2026-06-14.

**IP-5.** [Stated] Anchor: Bap cluster / baptism section ; cross-ref FV-proximity Strong objective baptismal regeneration stated plainly: (1) baptismal regeneration is the "historic" position "held for 1,500 years" and the MAJORITY Reformation view (baptismal *efficacy* — elect regenerated / promised at baptism — is the weaker, "more fringe" form); (2) baptism effects "the regeneration of ALL who receive that baptism"; (3) baptism forgives ALL sins, past AND FUTURE — and Rome's view is rejected as TOO WEAK precisely because it forgives only past sins, requiring confession after mortal sin. Sproul," faulting them for following the "Princeton theologian tradition" that waters the sacraments down "essentially [to] the same way your average baptist would be." **IP-7.** [Stated] + [Clarify] Anchor: new Eucharist section ; cross-ref §31-tension Eucharist: (1) REAL PRESENCE affirmed — "All of the Reformers, except for Zwingli… held to some form of real presence… you're receiving the body and blood of Christ"; more than "a spiritual benefit." (2) "SACRIFICE OF THE MASS" affirmed as UNION with the one sacrifice, not re-sacrifice — "not the re-sacrificing of Christ… the bringing to the present the one sacrifice of Christ so that we may be united to that sacrifice." (3) Sympathetic to Trent's rejection of re-sacrifice and to Anglican–RC rapprochement; "post-Vatican II, the Roman Church has become more proximate." [Clarify] Test against Art. 28 (body "given, taken, and eaten… only after an heavenly and spiritual manner… the mean… is Faith") and Art. 31 ("sacrifices of Masses… blasphemous fables and dangerous deceits"). RJ fences himself on the right side of Art. 31 by disclaiming re-sacrifice, but the "sacrifice of the Mass" vocabulary + Rome-proximate rhetoric is a Romeward-leaning pressure point to probe. — added 2026-06-15, from IP session 2026-06-14.

"Tradition is not a bad word… There is proper authority within tradition" (cites Chemnitz's seven kinds, rejecting only papal tradition). ## §13 / Incense — NEW [Analysis]: the priesthood-mediation refinement, and Luke 1:9-10 entering the corpus (260723-1)

**⚠️ ATTRIBUTION: this entry is [Analysis] in full. Nothing here is Stated or
Stated-Analysis.** It originates from an **external critique of the project's
incense reasoning** (260723). **The critique is a reviewer, not a source: no
source tag was created for it, and none may be created retroactively.** RJ has
said nothing on any of the material below; it is a refinement of JD's own
argument, logged here so the downstream documents have a ledger anchor.

**THE REFINEMENT.** The fulfillment argument had been running in a broad form
("fulfilled symbols cease") that carries a clean and probably fatal reply: *OT
believers prayed, prayer pre-existed the incense and continues after it, so a
reality pre-existing its symbol cannot show the symbol ceased.* The refined
claim is not vulnerable to that: **incense did not symbolize prayer
*simpliciter*, but prayer offered THROUGH the Levitical priesthood, under an
administration of restricted access.** The continuing reality is prayer; the
**fulfilled** thing is **the priestly mediation of prayer.**

**LUKE 1:9-10 — NEW TO THE CORPUS, 260723-1.** First appearance in any project
document. Zacharias's lot was to burn incense within, while "the whole multitude
of the people were praying without at the time of incense." The text itself
separates the people's prayer from the priest's incense act: same hour, two
places, a wall between, and **the people's prayer required no censer.** So the
smoke was not standing for bare prayer, which was already ascending from the
courtyard without it. Logged as high-value because it is a **narrative** datum
rather than a doctrinal inference, in a text RJ has no stake in resisting.
Supporting texts already in the corpus and now gathered under the same head:
**Heb 10:19-22** (the restricted access named as the thing removed — promoted
from rejoinder to premise), **Heb 7:12** (change of priesthood, change of law),
**Lev 16:12-13** (the weightiest incense act inside the Day of Atonement complex
Heb 9 declares fulfilled), **Num 16:46-48** (incense as priestly intercession).

**THE PRINCIPLE, NARROWED. ⚠️ Do not run the broad form.** Baptism and the
Lord's Supper are the standing counterexamples to "fulfilled symbols cease" and
a sharp interlocutor produces them at once. Deployable form: **"Old Covenant
symbols attached to the Levitical priesthood cease unless Christ or the apostles
positively reinstitute them under the New Covenant."** The reinstitution clause
absorbs both counterexamples — they continue because Christ instituted them by
name, not because fulfillment spared them. **Note the intramural property: the
narrow principle is DQ-4-compatible**, being the positive-warrant rule applied
to ceremonial carryover, which RJ affirmed on the record ("Correct"). It
therefore imports no contested Reformed premise, which places it in the same
portable class as the §2.5 asymmetry levers and the DQ-7 Bucket A finding.
Illustrative analogy held in reserve: **circumcision** — faith preceded it and
outlives it, yet circumcision ceased, because it signified covenant membership
under an administration rather than faith as such.

**DOWNSTREAM.** Developed at `RJ_Incense_Analysis.md` §4.12 (with §10.4
reordered to lead with the priesthood argument); staged as question **1e /
`Q-Inc-5`** in the question list, **not posted**; encoded in the peer-review
outline at Steps 5, 5b, and 6. **Funnel discipline unchanged — incense does not
enter the Discord thread until the filter is on the record, and DQ-5 remains
outstanding.**

## Baptism / sacramental objectivity — NEW: RJ contra the "Princeton tradition"  
[Stated — IP (session 2026-06-14)] Discussing justification (he sides with Calvin/the Reformed over the Lutherans here), RJ volunteered a sharp distinction between himself and what he called the "Princeton theologian tradition," naming James White, John MacArthur, and "even R.C. Sproul": that tradition waters the sacraments down until a Reformed baptism functions essentially as a Baptist one ("are you guys just baptists who are baptizing babies?"), with efficacy deferred to a later profession of faith. Against it he asserts "an objectivity to the sacraments that are meant to be promises for us and assurances for us." Illustrated with a PCA anecdote: friends who "almost make an apology for infant baptisms... just to let you guys know, this baptism doesn't save... nothing really is happening different to the child."  
Verbatim anchors: "I don't call myself a Calvinist, but I am far more of a Calvinist than James White, John MacArthur, even R.C. Sproul. Because they follow what's called this Princeton theologian tradition that the sacraments are so watered down... that they are essentially the same way your average baptist would be." / "There's an objectivity to the sacraments that are meant to be promises for us and assurances for us." / [PCA] "they'll be like, just to let you guys know, this baptism doesn't save... but he's got to make a profession of faith when he becomes of age. It's like, are you guys just baptists who are baptizing babies?"  
Classification: Bucket B, baptism cluster. CONFIRMS the standing finding that the primary RJ baptism disagreement is *baptismal regeneration/objectivity (Federal Vision proximity), not mode* — a clean, in-his-own-voice instance.

[Analysis — for JD] Do NOT inherit his figure-conflation: of the three he names, only Sproul is in the actual Hodge/Warfield Old Princeton (Presbyterian, paedobaptist) line; MacArthur is a credobaptist, White is Reformed Baptist. "Princeton tradition" is doing loose work as a label for "low-sacrament Reformed/evangelical broadly." Note too that his "Princeton" complaint is *sacramental*, NOT methodological — it has no bearing on the regulative-principle argument (which is Westminster/Puritan in origin, not Old-Princeton); if he ever waves off the RPW by gesturing at "Princeton rationalism," that is a different "Princeton" and a category error. Deeper in-person lever: his insistence that God (not the worshiper) defines and fills the sacrament shares a root with WCF 21.1 on worship (God institutes, we receive) — he can't consistently borrow Westminster's high sacramentology while discarding Westminster's worship theology; they issue from one document.

## §Formularies — METHOD NOTE: which Articles text is authoritative for RJ (controls all Bucket A)  
[Analysis — verified this session] RJ uses the American 1928 BCP, which prints the 1801 American revision of the Articles, not the 1571/1662 English text. The 1801 revision is POLITICAL, not doctrinal. Changes confined to: Art. 21 (Authority of General Councils) omitted entirely (church-state; side-effect drops the "councils may err" clause); Art. 8 removes the Athanasian Creed from creeds to be "thoroughly received"; Art. 37 (Civil Magistrates) replaced with a moderate-Calvinist church/state statement for the US; Art. 35 (Homilies) adds a gloss receiving the Homilies "so far as... an explication of Christian doctrine, and instructive in piety and morals," setting aside English constitutional references.  
DECISIVE: Articles 28, 31, and 34 — the entire spine of the incense/altar/vestments/Mass leverage — were NOT altered in 1801 and were carried into the 1928 BCP unchanged (the 1928 Convention rejected all revision proposals; Articles printed with the same 1801 prefatory language). Net effect on research to date: essentially none.  
Operating rule: (1) cite Articles 28/31/34 as RJ's OWN text ("Article 31, as printed in your 1928 Book of Common Prayer") — rhetorically STRONGER than 1662, forecloses any "that's the English version" deflection; (2) do NOT rest weight on the altered articles (8, 21, 37); (3) on Art. 35/Homilies lean on the surviving clause (received as instructive Christian doctrine) — enough to make the Homily Against Peril of Idolatry a witness to received Anglican doctrine, but do NOT claim it strictly binding; the American gloss softens its force slightly vs. 1662 subscription, so this lever is marginally softer against an 1801/1928 Episcopalian, though still real; (4) keep CR / 1571-1662 Articles / WCF as OUR ground, cite the 1928 Articles only as HIS binding text at points of identity — frame is "by your own standard," not "a standard we now jointly adopt," which avoids importing any weakened 1928 elements.

## In-Person Finding — Baptism cluster (the "Princeton" objection)

*Cluster: Baptism (sacramental objectivity / Federal Vision proximity). Source: IP (in-person, 2026), session 2026-06-14.*

## **New finding (baptism cluster)**

**RJ on the "Princeton" tradition and sacramental objectivity (IP, 2026-06-14).**

In discussing justification (where he sides with Calvin/the Reformed over the Lutherans), RJ volunteered a sharp distinction between himself and what he called the "Princeton theologian tradition," naming James White, John MacArthur, and "even R.C. Sproul." His claim, verbatim anchors below: that tradition waters the sacraments down until a Reformed baptism functions essentially as a Baptist one ("are you guys just baptists who are baptizing babies?"), with efficacy deferred to a later profession of faith. Against this he asserts "an objectivity to the sacraments that are meant to be promises for us and assurances for us." Illustrated with a PCA anecdote: friends who "almost make an apology for infant baptisms... just to let you guys know, this baptism doesn't save... nothing really is happening different to the child."

**Verbatim anchors:**

* "I don't call myself a Calvinist, but I am far more of a Calvinist than James White, John MacArthur, even R.C. Sproul. Because they follow what's called this Princeton theologian tradition that the sacraments are so watered down... that they are essentially the same way your average baptist would be."  
* "There's an objectivity to the sacraments that are meant to be promises for us and assurances for us."  
* [PCA anecdote] "They'll be like, just to let you guys know, this baptism doesn't save. And yes, the child here, nothing really is happening different to the child, but he's got to make a profession of faith when he becomes of age. It's like, are you guys just baptists who are baptizing babies?"

**Classification:** Bucket B (cross-tradition Reformed-vs-Anglican disagreement), baptism cluster. Confirms the standing project finding that the primary disagreement with RJ on baptism is **baptismal regeneration / objectivity (Federal Vision proximity), not mode.** This is a clean, sourced in-his-own-voice instance of that axis.

**Analyst notes (do not present as RJ's view):**

1. **Figure-conflation flag.** RJ groups White, MacArthur, and Sproul under "Princeton tradition." Only Sproul is in the actual Hodge/Warfield Old Princeton (Presbyterian, paedobaptist) line. MacArthur is a credobaptist; White is Reformed Baptist. So "Princeton tradition" functions here as a loose label for "low-sacrament Reformed/evangelical broadly," not the historical Old Princeton school. Worth noting so we don't inherit the conflation in our own analysis.  
2. **WCF leverage (his own potential ally, not just his target).** The high-efficacy reading RJ wants is not un-Westminster: WCF 28.6 holds that grace is really exhibited and conferred by the Spirit in baptism, in God's appointed time. RJ can plausibly claim to be *more* confessionally Reformed than the low-sacrament popularizers on this one axis. The live question for our cluster is whether RJ goes *past* WCF 28.6 toward ex opere / Federal Vision objectivity (efficacy detached from faith), which is where the actual disagreement sits. Diagnostic follow-up still open.  
3. **Cross-link to incense/RPW (Cross-Batch Reconciliation candidate).** RJ's "Princeton" complaint is *sacramental*, not methodological — it has no bearing on the regulative-principle argument (A1/B13), which is Westminster/Puritan in origin, not Old-Princeton. Note the deeper point for in-person: his insistence that God (not the worshiper) defines and fills the sacrament shares a root with WCF 21.1's logic on worship (God institutes, we receive). He cannot consistently borrow Westminster's high sacramentology while discarding Westminster's worship theology — they issue from one document. Hold as an in-person lever; do not put in a public post.

**Open question (add to OQ tracker):**

* OQ-[next]: Does RJ's sacramental "objectivity" stay within WCF 28.6 (grace conferred by the Spirit, in God's time, received by faith), or move past it toward Federal-Vision/ex-opere efficacy detached from faith? Probe with the baptism-efficacy diagnostic in person.

## Discord Question-Thread Findings (DQ ledger)

*Source: **DQ** = Discord question thread. DQ-1 … DQ-6 from the thread posted 2026-07-09 through 2026-07-15; RJ's substantive replies are dated 2026-07-09. Numbering continues unbroken from the established source-tag series. Same ledger discipline as the IP block above: each entry carries an anchor pointer rather than being folded into the section body.*

**DQ-1.** [Stated] Anchor: §Formularies / OQ formulary-authority (GATING for Bucket A) — **Formulary self-contradictions, enumerated.** Asked to list the self-contradictions he sees in the Thirty-Nine Articles and any exceptions he takes, RJ answered (Discord, 2026-07-09, 4:46 PM) that the tensions are "amongst the whole of the Formularies: the Prayer Book, the Articles, and the Books of Homilies," and "are not so clearly evident apart from their context." **Instance 1:** "The more Lutheran understanding of the Sacrament is seen in the Liturgy, Catechism, and some aspects of the Homilies, and the more explicitly Calvinist understanding is seen mostly in the last Article inserted: Article XXIX (inserted in 1571, after excommunication by the Bishop of Rome)." He adds the history: Article XXIX "was actually controversial in its day; the more Reformed party had tried to insert it earlier in 1563, but it was removed. When it was reinserted in 1571, it was done so at the opposition of Bishop Edmund Guest and others." **Instance 2:** "Article VI's understanding of the Apocrypha with the Books of Homilies constant reference to the Apocrypha." Article VI "maintains a purposefully ambiguous state for the Apocrypha, stating that the Books therein cannot be cited alone to support doctrinal claims, but not outright denying their (at least Deuterocanonical) canonicity," while the Homilies "freely reference them (always with Protocanonical Texts), using terms like, 'the Holy Ghost Spake in Tobit, saying.'" He offered exact examples once he has his physical copy to hand. **Addendum (5:49 PM):** the formularies "were made over the course of a century" (Prayer Book earliest aspects 1544, full 1549, official 1662; Homilies c.1540s-1570s; Articles 1550s-1570s), i.e. "over one century of development."

> ⭐⭐ **Dated note, 260808-1 — THE PROMISED HOMILY CITATION WAS DELIVERED, IN CLASS, TEN DAYS LATER.** At `A101-2026-07-19` (**`IP-20`**), with the Books of Homilies physically in the room, he supplied an exact instance-2 citation — Second Book of Homilies, the Homily of Alms-deeds (*"A homily 11"* per the `[S]` capture), the *"Holy Ghost also teach[es]"* passage, citing **Tobit, Proverbs and Sirach** — **together with a harmonization** (the deuterocanon cited as *supplemental*, alongside and in agreement with the protocanon, never as itself sufficient; his own Lancelot Andrewes analogy). ⚠️ **Delivered in class, not in this thread; the thread's promise stands discharged in substance, not in place.** ⛔ **The enumeration itself does not move, the downgraded closure question is NOT bumped, and the tension-vs-harmony question (`DQ-1` called it a self-contradiction; `IP-20` teaches the reconciling mechanism) is logged with BOTH frames his and NEITHER chosen.** Full entry and dual-capture verification at `IP-20`.

Articles 20 and 34, and the worship-related Homilies (esp. "Against the Peril of Idolatry"), **pass through the self-contradictions hedge ungated**. The Bucket A worship levers remain available. Note also that **the exceptions half of the question went unanswered** — he listed tensions only. That half remains open, and the posted closure question (Question List v12) is aimed at locking the enumeration.
