RC1-7 (explicit denial of juridical subscription) and GV-37 (1662 BCP named as the benchmark prayer books "are supposed to conform theologically to") continue to govern the framing: *your formularies / what you affirm / the standard you name*.

**DQ-2.** [Stated] Anchor: §6 (Sacraments — Number & Definition) ; cross-ref IP-4, GV-24/39, Q7 — **Article 25 and the seven sacraments.** RJ (Discord, 2026-07-09): "We separate them by pointing to the two as Dominical/Gospel, as their Signs are given/commanded directly by our Lord, and pertain to the Forgiveness of sins, and the Five Ecclesial Sacraments as developing from the Life of the Church, rooted in Apostolic Tradition. The Five are not of the same level and kind as the Two. The Five can be called 'Sacraments', so long as they are not seen as Sacraments of the Gospel." He grounds this in the Second Book of Homilies, "Common Prayer and Sacraments Ought to Be Ministered in a Tongue That is Understanded of the Hearers," quoting it at length, including its statements that on the exact signification "there be but two, namely, Baptism, and the Supper of the Lord"; that "in a general acception the name of a Sacrament may be attributed to any thing whereby an holy thing is signified," a class the Homily extends to "oil, washing of feet, and such like"; and that the other rites retained by the Church of England are to be taken "either for godly states of life… or else judged to be such ordinances as may make for the instruction, comfort, and edification of Christ's Church."

> **[Analysis] RETIRE THE LEVER.** This is a formulary-faithful answer. The Article 25 lever moves to the do-not-deploy register alongside Lent and baptismal regeneration (Question List v12).
>
> **[Analysis] Two residues worth logging.** First, **the grace half of the question was not answered**: whether the Five *confer grace* is untouched, and that is where the Roman difference actually lives (Trent: seven, all conferring grace *ex opere operato*, all instituted by Christ). His answer is compatible with "the Five confer grace, just not the forgiveness tied to a Dominical sign." Second, there is a gap between the Homily's deflationary "general acception" (a class covering foot-washing and oil) and his capitalized "Ecclesial Sacraments… developing from the Life of the Church, rooted in Apostolic Tradition," which is a **positive dogmatic category the Homily does not supply**. Staged as a soft follow-up (Question List v12, Bucket C).
>
> **[Analysis] METHOD DATUM (raises the value of Homily-based material generally).** He treats the Homilies as his **authoritative interpretive lens on the Articles**. This lifts the standing of every Homily-anchored lever in the project, including "Against the Peril of Idolatry" (§12, Q2, QC-b).

**DQ-3.** [Stated] Anchor: §13 (Worship Theology & the Regulative Principle) / OQ8 ; cross-ref IP-2, BP-41 — **RPW "rightly understood": the five-example answer.** Asked where the typical confessional understanding of the RPW gets it wrong and what he would correct, RJ (Discord, 2026-07-09, 5:20 PM) defined "the most extreme I can think of" (exclusive Psalms, required a capella, no images/crosses, no worship except Sundays, no Feast Days including Christmas and Easter, no recitation of Creeds) and refuted it in five numbered points:
>
> 1. "Psalms are not exclusively required. Matthew 26:30 shows our Lord and the Apostles singing an hymn together."
> 2. "A capella is not required. Psalm 150 makes little sense in light of the fact that it lists all sorts of instruments for praise. The counter to this is that praise is not the same as worship. **The problem is that praise is an element of worship**, and the Psalm (and the rest of Scripture) does not say, 'Praise Him with these instruments, unless it's in the form of worship.'"
> 3. "Images are all throughout the worship of the Old Testament, and even commanded by God, from the bronze serpent (Numbers 21:4-9) to the Temple itself (1 Kings 6; 2 Chronicles 3), to the Ark of the Covenant." Cherubim on the ark (Exod 25:18-22); Joshua and the elders "rightly bowed down before the Ark" (Josh 7:6); the ark as "the footstool of our God" (1 Chron 28:2); bowing before the footstool (Ps 99:5; 132:7-8). "We are not to bow to the images in the sense of obeisance to them, but to the untrained eye seeing Joshua and the Elders bow before the Presence of the Lord at the Ark would look like bowing to the images of the Cherubim."
> 4. Not Sunday-only: daily gathering (Acts 2:46-47); apostolic temple worship (Acts 3:1) and synagogue attendance (Acts 13:14-15; 17:1-3); and "Christ Himself participated in 'extrabiblical' Feast Days: namely, He participated in the Feast of Dedication, Hannukah, which comes from 1 Maccabees 4:52-59 (this is found in John 10:22-23). So according to the Biblical witness, **Feast Days can be added to the Calendar apart from Divine Command**."
> 5. On creeds: opposing recitation because "the exact word-order is not directly found in Scripture would be like opposing a homily or a prayer because the exact word-order is not directly found in Scripture." Notes the early Puritan petition to King James VI and I opposing the Canticles (Nunc Dimittis, Magnificat, Benedictus) for not being Psalms.

> **[Stated-Analysis]** He did not engage the mainstream three-bucket Westminster version, and **did not state a positive rule of his own**. The answer is a refutation of a caricature.
>
> **[Analysis] ELEMENT VOCABULARY — standing attribution rule updated.** Point 2 is the **first logged instance of RJ using "element" as a term of art**: "praise is an element of worship." He demonstrably speaks the taxonomy. **He has still never applied "element" to incense**; that classification remains **project Analysis**, not Stated. The rule changes only in this respect: it is no longer available to say he does not use the vocabulary.
>
> **[Analysis] METHOD FINDING (high value).** **Four of the five rebuttals argue from POSITIVE WARRANT.** Hymns by dominical example (Matt 26:30). Instruments by command (Ps 150). Images by command (bronze serpent, cherubim, temple). Creeds by necessary-inference-style reasoning (forms of commanded acts). Only point 4's Hanukkah move argues from permission. This is **the confessional RPW method deployed by RJ himself**, and it licenses posing the incense question in his own idiom: "you defended images by pointing to where God commanded them; where is incense commanded, and what did the command regulate?"
>
> **[Analysis] His targets are largely not Westminster positions.** WCF 21.5 provides for solemn fastings and thanksgivings on special occasions, so "Sunday-only" is not the confessional view; confessional Presbyterians recite creeds and sing composed hymns as *forms* of commanded elements; JD's own position already allows instruments and newly composed hymns. **His stated corrections leave the version of the RPW used in the incense argument untouched.**
>

**DQ-8.** [Stated] ★★ Anchor: §13 / OQ8 ; **answers DQ-5** ; cross-ref DQ-4, DQ-9, IP-3, Rev-9/10/11 — **THE OT-CARRYOVER FILTER, ANSWERED.** Twenty minutes after JD posted the crux question, RJ replied (Discord, **2026-07-10, 11:06 PM**), verbatim and in full:

> *"By looking at what we have received as the consensus-form of worship, and comparing it to what we see espoused in Scripture. For instance, we do have the Passover Lamb as central to our worship. Christ is also our priest. Both of these are strongly in the New Testament."*

> **[Stated]** His filter is **two-stage**: (i) *the received consensus-form of worship* supplies the candidate practice; (ii) *comparison with what Scripture espouses* tests it. Worked examples given: the **Passover Lamb**, "central to our worship," and **Christ as priest** — both, he says, "strongly in the New Testament."
>
> **[Analysis] — order of operations is the whole finding.** Under **DQ-4** (which he affirmed with "Correct") the question is *where is this warranted?*; Scripture supplies the candidate and the practice must be shown to have warrant. Under **DQ-8** the question is *is what we have received contradicted?*; tradition supplies the candidate and Scripture serves as a check on it. **These are not the same test**, and the gap between them is precisely the regulative/normative fork. This is not a gotcha and must not be run as one — it is the most natural thing in the world for a high-church pastor to say, and he plainly does not experience the two as different. But it is the seam, it is intramural, and it needs no contested Reformed premise: only his own DQ-4 answer and his own DQ-8 answer side by side.
>
> **⚠️ [Analysis] — THE HIGH-VALUE FINDING: his own two examples model fulfilment-by-antitype, not carryover.** Look at what each example actually does. The Passover Lamb is "central to our worship" **because Christ is the Passover** — the OT ceremonial act (the slaughter and eating of a literal lamb) is *not* retained; its antitype is. "Christ is also our priest" **concedes that the Levitical priesthood does not survive** — again, the antitype is retained and the OT office is not. **Neither example is a case of an Old Covenant ceremonial *act* being carried into New Covenant worship in material form.** Both are cases of a type terminating in Christ. So **his own filter, applied to his own worked examples, produces the Reformed result** — which is exactly the argument the project runs against material incense, where Rev 5:8 names the antitype (the prayers of the saints) in the text itself.
>
> **⚠️ [Analysis] — Heb 7:12 conceded in his own words.** "Christ is also our priest," offered as his own example of correct OT carryover, is the load-bearing premise of the **priesthood-mediation refinement** staged on 260723-1 (§13 entry; question list item **1e / `Q-Inc-5``**; `RJ_Incense_Analysis.md` §4.12). That refinement needed him to grant that the Levitical priesthood is fulfilled and superseded rather than continued. **He has now granted it unprompted, in a neutral context, before incense was ever mentioned.** This is the strongest single datum the funnel has acquired, and it was acquired at zero cost.
>
> **[Analysis] — do not overstate.** He has *not* said that every OT ceremonial act must terminate in an antitype, and he would not accept that as a stated rule. The finding is that **his own chosen examples exhibit that pattern**, which makes the pattern askable as a question — *"both of your examples look like cases where the Old Testament thing is fulfilled in Christ rather than continued; is that the pattern, or are there cases where the practice itself carries forward?"* — and unaskable as an allegation.

**DQ-9.** [Stated] ★★ Anchor: §13 / OQ8 ; cross-ref DQ-4, DQ-8, DQ-3, EXT-Cooper — **THE MILK-AND-HONEY REFINEMENT: "PRINCIPLES AND NOT INDIVIDUAL ACTS."** Pressed by JD (07-11, 8:14 AM) on whether a practice well established in the received consensus but absent from Scripture would pass on consensus alone, RJ answered (Discord, **2026-07-11, 8:43 AM**) with the milk-and-honey hypothetical: some early Christians gave milk and honey to the newly baptized; *supposing that became a universal tradition,* he does not believe it would violate a proper understanding of the RPW, **"because the RPW is about principles and not individual acts."** His stated complaint: others use the RPW "for individual practices, demanding those EXACT practices be found in Scripture, rather than principles that are drawn from the witness of Scripture." **His stated principle:** *"that imagery and symbolism are to reflect the Biblical witness"* — milk and honey point to the Promised Land, which ties to Baptism and to the Old Testament. **DQ-10.** [Stated] ★ Anchor: §13 / §12 ; cross-ref DQ-9, DQ-7, RC3-8, BP-38 — **THE BOUNDARY ANSWER: ONE EXCLUSION, PRODUCED BY A DIFFERENT RULE.** Asked directly (JD, 07-11 3:48 PM) for an example of a practice his imagery-and-symbolism principle would **exclude**, RJ answered (Discord, **2026-07-11, 11:22 PM**), in a single sentence: *"I do not find a principle in Scripture that would allow for prayers to the Saints, so that would be one example."* Pressed (JD, 07-12) on what specifically blocks it, he replied (**2026-07-21, 12:04 AM**) in two numbered points: **(1)** he does not see how Rev 5:8 and 8:3-4 prove that petitioning the saints directly is appropriate — "There seems to be a leap there" from *the prayers of the saints are received in Heaven as a part of the worship* to *therefore we can pray to particular Saints… in some supernatural way and that it is good to do so*; **(2)** *"What blocks my usage of prayers to the Saints in Heaven is that prayer is always seen as an act of worship and as directed to God alone."*

> **⚠️ [Analysis] — THE MOST DEPLOYABLE FINDING IN THIS BATCH.** Read point (2) carefully. **The exclusion is not produced by the imagery principle.** It is produced by an entirely separate rule about the proper *object* of worship. So when the imagery-and-symbolism principle was asked, directly and in the friendliest possible terms, to produce a single exclusion, **it produced none** — the one case offered is ruled out on other grounds and would be ruled out by anybody, on any principle, including a strict normative-principle Anglican.
>
> **The consequence, stated carefully:** a principle that licenses practices and excludes none is a **permission-generator, not a filter**. That is the normative principle under a different name — the very position RJ has explicitly declined (he called it "too loose," IP-2/DQ-3, and affirmed positive warrant at DQ-4). **Intramural; needs no Reformed premise; runs entirely on his own three answers.**
>
> **Deployment form — clarification, never charge, and the wording matters:** *"Is there anything the imagery principle itself rules out — some practice that genuinely does reflect a biblical image, but that you'd still exclude? I ask because prayers to the saints seem to be ruled out by the second thing you said, that prayer is worship and belongs to God alone, which I'd agree with, rather than by the imagery test itself. I'm trying to see what work the imagery principle is doing on its own."* This is a continuation of a question JD has already asked once, not a new line of pressure, which is what makes it natural rather than pointed.
>
> **[Analysis] — the "leap" in point (1): handle with precision, do NOT overstate.** It is tempting to read point (1) as RJ rejecting depiction-to-practice inference as such, which would be the perfect mirror of the project's incense argument. **That reading is wrong and must not be deployed.** His **DQ-7** answer ("It is the first") says the opposite: depiction of an approved or uncondemned example *does* generate obligation. His objection here is narrower and text-specific — that **Rev 5:8 does not depict prayer *to* the saints at all**, which he grounds in the genitive (see DQ-7a note below on the Greek). So the leap he names is a leap from a **misread text**, not from depiction to practice.

**LS-84.** [Stated] Anchor: **§Formularies** ⭐⭐⭐ *(secondary: §2)* ; cross-ref `RC1-7` ⭐⭐⭐, `DQ-1`, `LS-11`, `LS-20`, `LS-74`, `LS-83`, `GV-43`, `VP-1` **(FLAG ONLY)**, OQ row 9, `RJ_Open_Questions_and_Divergences.md` §2 row 5 — ⭐⭐⭐ **THE SUBSCRIPTION QUESTION PUT TO HIM DIRECTLY AND ANSWERED: NOT MERELY *NOT REQUIRED* BUT ***TECHNICALLY IMPOSSIBLE*** — AND HE SAYS THE CORPUS *"DOES NEED TO BE CLEANED UP."*** ⛔⛔ **THE QUESTION IS A VIEWER'S, READ ALOUD, AND IS THE FILE'S ONLY OCCURRENCE OF `required`: *"are anglicans required to hold 100% of the Articles, books and homilies? @84,042 [44:33]; @84,338 [44:39]; @84,433 [44:41]; @85,796 [45:24]. `DATE:` **2023-03-04.** **ATTRIBUTION: HIS ANSWER ONLY — the question is a viewer's, read aloud, and is quoted here as the viewer's.** **[Analysis]** ⭐⭐⭐ **THE PROJECT'S STANDING CALIBRATION IS TESTED AT ITS SHARPEST POINT AND IT HOLDS — AND SHARPENS.** The calibration says he has never called the formularies *binding* and explicitly denies juridical subscription (`RC1-7`, `VP-1`). ⭐⭐ **A video titled *"The Importance of a Confessional Standard"* was the most direct available test of it, and the answer he gives to the question put to him is not merely *"no one requires it"* but ***"technically you can't"*** — a claim about the corpus rather than about church discipline. ⛔⛔ **THAT IS STRONGER THAN THE CALIBRATION, NOT WEAKER, AND THE GUARD MUST NOT BE RELAXED ON THE STRENGTH OF THE VIDEO'S TITLE.** ⭐⭐ **What IS new, and belongs to the record rather than to any lever, is the reformist half: *"this does need to be cleaned up"* — he thinks the incoherence is a defect to be repaired, not a feature to be defended.** ⚠️ **`LS-95` records the 2023-11 version of the same thought (a *"more detailed confessional standard maybe"*, *"revisit the Articles… the prayer book… the books of homilies"*).** ⛔ **He has never been asked what a cleaned-up standard would say about anything in Bucket A, and constructing that question's answer for him is what the attribution discipline forbids.** ⛔ **DECLINED at §15.**

**LS-85.** [Stated] Anchor: **§2 Scripture & Authority** ⭐⭐ *(secondary: §Formularies)* ; cross-ref `LS-83`, `LS-84`, `LS-95`, `LS-23`, `RC-5` — ⭐⭐ **WHY A CONFESSIONAL STANDARD MATTERS AT ALL, IN HIS OWN WORDS AND FROM A WORKED EXAMPLE — AND THE ADMISSION THAT NO STANDARD, HOWEVER TIGHT, SETTLES EVERYTHING.** The occasion is a social-media argument in which an interlocutor could not define limited atonement from any confession he held: *"can you give me a definition of limited atonement from a confessional standard to which you hold?"* — and *"he didn't really have one"*, *"he was holding on to sort of his own understanding of things"* (@3,452 [01:53]). ⭐ **The principle: without one, *"people will be talking past each other, or people will be moving targets, and they'll tell you one moment this is what they believe [and] in another that's what they believe"* (@6,459 [03:33]); what a confession does is make theology *"concrete"* and *"well-defined"* (@5,559 [03:02]).** ⭐⭐ **And the limit, stated against his own interest and repeated four times: *"there's going to be differences no matter how tight your confessional standards are"* — Lutherans differ on the Eucharist, Roman Catholics differ on the Eucharist and on predestination *"about as wide as… Calvin and… Molina"*, and Rome's magisterium is itself *"their… confessional standards"* (@58,379 [31:15], @58,554 [31:19]).** `SRC:` @3,452; @5,559; @6,459; @58,379; @58,554. `DATE:` **2023-03-04.** **ATTRIBUTION: solo video, certain.** **[Analysis]** ⭐⭐ **This is the video's thesis and it is the frame every other File 25 finding sits inside: a confessional standard is valuable as a PUBLIC DEFINITION that stops a position being a moving target — not as a juridical requirement.** ⛔⛔ **AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY IT DOES NOT LICENSE THE "BINDING" FRAMING: the work he wants the standard to do is definitional, not disciplinary.** ⚠️ **The tu-quoque about every tradition's internal differences is a real argument and is also the move that makes `LS-84`'s *"technically you can't"* survivable for him; the two are read together or not at all.**

**LS-86.** [Stated] Anchor: **§2 Scripture & Authority** ⭐⭐ *(secondary: §3 Councils)* ; cross-ref `LS-24` ⭐⭐⭐, `LS-40` ⭐⭐⭐, `IP-77` ⭐⭐, `RV-15`, `RC-5`, `LS-23`, OQ row 19 — ⭐⭐ **CHURCH AUTHORITY AFFIRMED, INFALLIBILITY DENIED, AND SUBMISSION STATED IN THE FIRST PERSON — ARTICLE XX TAUGHT, 2023.** Reading Article XX aloud he glosses it three ways. **First, the affirmation:** *"sola scriptura does not deny the authority of the church"*; *"we believe that the church has authority [in] controversies of faith"*; and, in the first person, *"if the church is determining something [in] a controversy in matters of dogma, as a Christian I am submitted to that authority"* (@38,282 [20:25], @38,746 [20:41], @41,246 [22:07]). **Second, the denial:** it *"just denies that the church's authority is infallible in any capacity"*; *"that does not mean it is [infallible]"*; *"believing in church authority… is not… a rejection of sola scriptura, nor is it a confession that the church is infallible"* (@38,282; @42,436 [22:43]). **Third, the limit, from the Article's own text:** the church may not *"ordain anything that is contrary to God's word written"* nor *"enforce anything to be believed for necessity of salvation"* beyond it. `SRC:` @38,282; @38,746; @41,246; @42,436. `DATE:` **2023-03-04.** **ATTRIBUTION: solo video, certain — ⛔ the Article XX text itself attributed to the Articles (§5 rule 9.4).** **[Analysis]** ⭐⭐ **`LS-40` (2024) and `IP-77` (2026) record authority-without-infallibility for councils; `LS-24` (2021) ranks the consensus above the Bishop of Rome. THIS is the same structure stated of THE CHURCH generally, from the Article, in 2023 — the middle term of that series and the only one that states his own SUBMISSION in the first person.** ⭐ **Credited at §15: an authority that binds without being infallible, bounded by Scripture, is the Anglican and the Reformed account both.** ⛔ **It does NOT move OQ row 19 (why the Bishop of Rome ranks as a tier) — `bishop of rome` 0 in this file — and it does NOT move Step 10: `burden` 0 and `consensus` 0 across all three files in this batch.**

**LS-89.** [Stated] Anchor: **§8 Eucharist — Presence** ⭐⭐ ; cross-ref `LS-76` ⭐⭐⭐ **(same batch, c. 2021)**, `IP-42`, `IP-53`, `IP-64`, `RC3-*`, `RJ_Open_Questions_and_Divergences.md` §2 row 2, QA-Euc — ⭐⭐ **THE WORD *"PHYSICALLY"* DECLINED IN 2023 — AND ⛔⛔ THIS IS NOT REPORTED AS A CHANGE FROM `LS-76`.** Asked whether he is *"a consubstantiation kind of guy"* he first refuses the term — *"consubstantiation is not a proper term to use; it demands that we hold to [an] Aristotelian metaphysics"* — then states the presence: *"truly the body and blood of Christ are there just as truly as the… bread and wine are there"* (@71,825 [37:55], @72,408 [38:14]). ⭐⭐ **He then corrects himself mid-sentence and declines *"physically"*: agreeing with a named Lutheran theologian who *"denied that the body and blood are physically present"*, he defines the term — *"think of physically as physics… constrained by time, space… the three dimensions"* — and concludes *"we wouldn't necessarily confess that it is, quote, physically present, because it's not contained within the physics… so that's why I had to correct myself there"* (@74,064 [39:18], @74,506 [39:33]). ⭐ **The positive statement stands unchanged: *"when I am eating the Holy Communion I am genuinely eating the body and blood of Christ… it is body, it is blood, which is also bread, which is also wine"* (@75,026 [39:51]); and *"sacramental union — that's the term I use often"* (@77,445 [41:07]).** `SRC:` @71,825; @72,408; @73,453; @74,064; @74,506; @75,026; @77,445. `DATE:` **2023-03-04.** **ATTRIBUTION: solo video, certain; the *"consubstantiation"* prompt is a viewer's.** **[Analysis]** ⚠️⚠️⚠️ **THIS IS THE BATCH'S SHARPEST INTERNAL TENSION AND IT IS LOGGED WITH BOTH READINGS LIVE AND NEITHER CHOSEN.** `LS-76` (c. 2021) has him saying ***"it can only be the physical body and the physical blood of Christ"***; this (2023) has him saying ***"we wouldn't necessarily confess that it is, quote, physically present."*** ⛔⛔ **BOTH READINGS ARE AVAILABLE AND NEITHER IS ADOPTED.** **(a) NOT A CONFLICT AT ALL — DIFFERENT TARGETS:** in `LS-76` he is refusing a *non-physical body* (an incarnational objection: Christ's body IS a physical body); here he is refusing *local dimensional containment* (a metaphysical objection: the body is not in the bread the way an object is in a box). ⭐ **He himself distinguishes the senses in both sources — `LS-76` s395: *"spiritual does not negate physical"*; here: *"think of physically as physics"* — and §2 row 2's *"physically united to the bread and the wine"* is the phrase both are circling.** **(b) A REAL NARROWING** between a c.-2021 conversation with a Reformed interlocutor and a 2023 solo answer. ⛔⛔ **DO NOT CHOOSE. He has not been asked, the two occasions had different opponents, and ⛔ "you used to say X" is precisely the sentence §5 rule 8.3 exists to prevent.** ⛔ **NO `VP-` PAIR, NO NUMBER, NO `DELTA`.**

**LS-92.** [Stated + Stated-Analysis] Anchor: **§7 Baptism / §11 Priesthood & Absolution** ⭐⭐⭐ *(secondary: §6)* ; cross-ref **Known Gap 11** ⭐⭐⭐, `POD-5`, `IP-33`, `IP-54`, `IP-64`, `IP-70`, `IP-78`, `RJ_Open_Questions_and_Divergences.md` §1 row 18 — ⭐⭐⭐ **KNOWN GAP 11's COMMUNION-PRECONDITION HALF GETS ITS FIRST DATUM IN ANY ERA, IN HIS OWN FIRST PERSON AS THE PRIEST ADMINISTERING.** He states his own admission criteria without being asked: *"I let parishioners know that you have to have been baptized, you have to confess, you have to have no unconfessed… sins"* — ⭐ **and he immediately names WHICH confession he means: *"and we obviously we do confession during the Liturgy itself"*, the object being *"no unrepentant sin at the very least"*** (@29,556 [15:37], @29,814 [15:45], @30,165 [15:58]). ⭐⭐ **The fourth criterion: *"you have to confess some sort of understanding of the real presence of Christ in the Eucharist"*** (@30,165). ⭐ **The governing principle is 1 Corinthians 11 and it is stated against his own prerogative: *"scripture itself says that a man should examine himself… before receiving communion, not necessarily to be examined by the priest"*, though *"there is [a] responsibility of the priest to make sure that… people should be properly receiving"* (@33,094 [17:22]).** ⭐⭐ **And the tie-breaker, twice: *"I would rather accept the person to receive communion rather than reject the person, because… if I deny somebody communion who should receive communion, I [am] literally denying that person Christ"*** (@31,753 [16:41], @32,589 [17:08]). ⭐ **Context he supplies himself: admitting the unconfirmed to communion is *"a more recent development… about the 60s or 70s"* and *"I actually think [it is] an appropriate position"* (@29,091 [15:20]).** `SRC:` @29,091; **BLOG-52.** [Stated] Anchor: §2 Scripture & Authority ; cross-ref RC4-1, RC4-3, RC4-4, RC4-6, RC4-7, RC4-2, DQ-1 — ⭐⭐⭐ **THE DEUTEROCANON POSITION, WHOLE, IN 2016 — AND IT IS THE `RC-4` POSITION TEN YEARS EARLY.** He prefers **"Deuterocanon"** to **"Apocrypha"** and says so explicitly, calling it the better name. He then qualifies **against himself**: the early church was **not uniform** on them, **Jerome** is a named exception among others, few if any Fathers rejected them entirely, and none to his knowledge thought them satanic. **The Anglican position he reports:** a *"lesser"* canon — **read in church services and used in study, but not of the same authority** as the NT or the universally received OT, so that a claim found **only** in Tobit cannot be taught as authoritative doctrine for the whole Church or as necessary for salvation.
